messages:
Alex: Quick async — what I did / blockers / today
Maya: nice, drop a short list of priorities?
Alex: did the KV eviction experiment on dedicated-POOL-A, results look better for 99p latency but cost up a bit. blocker: need decision on whether to keep warm-policy for low-traffic models.
Sam: can you paste the perf numbers?
Alex: logs + summary below:
```
kv-evict-run: dedicated-POOL-A
window=30m, warm_hits=72%, cold_miss_p95=189ms -> 120ms after warm-policy
cost_delta =~ +6% GPU-hours
```
Jordan: where are we seeing noise increased? any page spikes?
Alex: noise came from batcher 504s during the test ramp on the canary, correlated with eviction churn. opened SRE-231 to track.
Maya: SRE-231 assigned to Jordan? pinged you on the ticket.
Jordan: on it, will triage alerts and add a short playbook. planning to mute low-priority 504 alert for 2h during the next warm-policy rollout.
Lee: FYI ops-bot reported a canary rollout earlier that touched the same pool. ops-bot: Canary finished on dedicated-POOL-A, traffic ramp 10->40% over 12m.
ops-bot: Canary status: PASS in us-west-2, FAIL in eu-west-1 (kv timeout), tagging Jordan.
Sam: eu-west kv timeouts are the same pattern as last week — possible cross-regional DNS flaps. Jordan, can you correlate with network ops?
Jordan: will check with infra. quick mitigation: lower eviction aggressiveness and enable per-model prefix caching for the small models group.
Maya: for today: 1) Jordan to mute noisy 504 alerts + join infra for root cause. 2) Alex to draft recommendation (keep warm-policy / rollback) with cost delta and perf charts. 3) Sam to run a short load-run against eu-west kv nodes.
Alex: adding: need a one-paragraph blurb for the oncall handover in case this escalates overnight.
Sam: I can take the overnight window if it flaps after 22:00 UTC — I'll be reachable.
Lee: marking ops-runbook snippet for evict rollouts. Paste into the ticket: 
```
- If 504 spike after rollout: rollback to previous policy with:
  kubectl -n redwood rollout undo deploy/kv-evict-controller
- Temporarily mute alert: /mute alert kv-504-noisy for 2h
- Notify infra oncall: @infra-oncall
```
Maya: thanks. Alex — any blockers from console dashboards or tracing you need help with?
Alex: trace data is fine, just need someone to sanity-check the p95 numbers in the dashboard — Sam can you quick-verify?
Sam: on it, will post a screenshot in SRE-231.
Jordan: infra pinged back: there's a short DNS flapping window in eu-west that matches the timestamps. they'll drop a mitigant, ETA 90m.
Alex: ok — if infra mitigates, we'll keep warm-policy and monitor cost. if not, rollback plan ready.
Maya: great — please update SRE-231 and the oncall note before you sign off. :thumbsup:
Alex: will do. quick FYI for tomorrow: propose a short experiment to test prefix caching effectiveness for <5rps models.
Lee: sounds good. I'll add a calendar 30m sync if needed.
ops-bot: Reminder: nightly KV maintenance window scheduled at 02:00 UTC. Expect short reconnects.
Sam: thanks, noted.
Maya: that covers my side — no other blockers.
Alex: end of thread — thanks everyone.
